Guided trip

The strangest things we have ever sent

A family photograph, two golf balls, a library, a record and a car.

Open the trip: The strangest things we have ever sent

A photograph lying in the dust

His family signed the back and pressed their thumbprints into it. It also says: This is the family of Astronaut Duke from Planet Earth, who landed on the Moon on the twentieth of April 1972.

Two golf balls, twenty-four and forty yards out

They went twenty-four and forty yards, not the miles everybody repeats. The brand is unknown: Shepard never said, so that nobody could make money from it.

Thirty million pages, and some tardigrades

Nobody knows where in the wreck the discs ended up; the camera orbiting the Moon cannot pick them out. Nor can anyone say whether the tardigrades survived the crash.

A gold record, further away than anything

Bolted to the side of this spacecraft is a gold-plated record. It carries whale song, greetings in fifty-five languages, and one woman's heartbeat, recorded two days after she decided to get married.

A car, going round the Sun

In the glovebox, a towel and a copy of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy; on a circuit board, the words Made on Earth by humans. Nobody has actually looked at it since 2018.

And this is where all of it came from

Every one of those things was made by people standing on that. From out here you cannot pick it out of the dark.

Everything is drawn where it really is, from the planets’ own orbits (astronomy-engine).
